questions.learningObjective: compute equivalence-point volume in a strong titration
questions.stem: 40.65975605510175 mL of 0.272 M strong acid is titrated with 0.085 M strong base. What volume of base reaches the equivalence point?

options.misconception: mixes the quantities incorrectly instead of equating moles
swaps the acid and base molarities in the ratio
multiplies all three values rather than conserving moles

questions.explanation: At equivalence the moles of base added equal the moles of acid present initially. Solving M acid times V acid equals M base times V base for the base volume divides the acid mole product by the base molarity.
questions.hint: Equate moles of acid and base.

questions.stem: In the routine mass determination exercise below, a technician reports these measurements. Determine the pH at the equivalence point of a strong acid titrated with a strong base at 25 degrees Celsius?

questions.hint: Think about whether the salt ions hydrolyze.
